feat(explainer): vue-component blocks, rendered at build and hydrated as islands

## Intent

Data-driven exercises carry maths and some sciences, but a cell diagram to label or a circuit to switch needs real interface code. Pages that use such code must still read without JavaScript. This is step 5 of the explainer MVP.

## Key changes

- A vue-component block names a component in src/components/, gives its props and requires a nojs text in every language, which the page shows without JavaScript.
- The build renders each component on the server into a hidden island; in the browser it hydrates and replaces the nojs text, or keeps it as a caption if the component declares that. Only pages with a component load Vue.
- Props are checked against the component's declared types; a string prop is a learner text, checked in every language.
- Build checks with one line per problem: no network, no eval, innerHTML or v-html, imports only from allowed modules, browser globals only while mounted, a test file per component, 20 kB gzip per component.
- A component that emits answered is an exercise: its logic module exports generate, check, solution and wrong, property-tested over 50 seeds, and answered drives the quiz's feedback.
- explainerTests() checks each nojs text without JavaScript and, with JavaScript in German, that each component hydrates without errors.
- The history fixture gets a component where the learner labels a pyramid; vue and the Vue plugin are pinned, and vue-tsc type-checks .vue files in CI.
